//: Enforces the tokens-first rule from CLAUDE.md mechanically, because as a
convention alone it doesn't hold: colours, type sizes and radii drift back
to literals a few at a time, and each one looks harmless in isolation.
The allow-lists are deliberately narrow — a token reference or a keyword,
nothing else. If a value genuinely has no token, the fix is to add one to
src/styles/tokens.css and say what it's for, not to widen these lists.
All of the site's CSS is under src/styles/ — no .astro file carries a
<style> block, and test/styles.test.ts enforces that. The .astro override
below stays anyway: it costs nothing, and it means a reintroduced block is
linted rather than silently exempt in the window before the test is run.
Prettier owns formatting, so the non-token rules here are limited to
correctness — nothing stylistic that would duplicate or fight it.
Not covered: the `transition` shorthand, where a value allow-list can't
reach the duration/easing inside it — use --duration-* and --ease-* anyway
(the longhands are covered below). Keyframe animation choreography
(animations.css stagger delays, the hero drift) is deliberately exempt:
those timings are composition, not UI state, and a shared token would tie
unrelated animations together.
The shorthand rules (background, border-*, box-shadow, text-shadow) accept
any value that references a token — gradients built from --color-*-rgb
channels included — plus the structural keywords. A raw colour anywhere in
them fails.
The `color` list additionally refuses --color-moss, --color-moss-2 and
--color-clay by name. They are brand colours, not text colours: none of
them reaches 4.5:1 on any surface the site uses. Reach for --color-moss-ink
or --color-clay-ink for type, and leave the full-strength pair for rules,
borders and marks. This is a lint rather than a review note because the
failure is invisible — the wrong token looks like the right one.
Not covered here either: an accent used as a *fill* under white text, which
is the same contrast pair inverted and needs the ink too (see .btn). A value
allow-list can't see the pairing, so test/contrast.test.ts checks the
numbers and this comment carries the rule.
